items.text:
Your LinkedIn headline is probably just your job title. Try this:

"My headline: [title]. What I actually do: [one line]. Rewrite it 5 ways: results-first, recruiter keywords, one line people remember, for freelance clients, plain and confident. Max 120 characters each. Don't add numbers I didn't give you."

For a marketing coordinator who runs email + social for 6 dental offices, my pick was:
"I write the emails your dentist sends. All 6 offices."

The last rule keeps it from inventing stats.

items.text:
"Make it better" might be the worst prompt you can type.

Better for who? Shorter or longer? The AI has to guess, and it usually guesses longer and fancier.

Add one line: who's reading it and what they should do next. Most rewrites get fixed right there.

What's a prompt you quit using because it never worked?

items.text:
Night-before-Thanksgiving group text, before:
"hey so tomorrow is at 3 but maybe 3:30 idk, can someone bring chairs?? also who's doing pie, and is anyone vegetarian this year"

Prompt: "Turn this into one clear group text. Keep my facts. End with the questions people need to answer."

After:
"Tomorrow starts at 3, maybe 3:30. Quick questions:
1. Who can bring chairs?
2. Who's doing pie?
3. Anyone vegetarian this year?"

More everyday prompts, free: https://makc9k.gumroad.com/l/starter10
